title: Autonomous Agents for Scientific Tasks - Sina Shahandeh, Radicait
talk_summary: Sina Shahandeh describes how coding agents saturate on open-ended optimization problems because they run out of hypotheses, not implementation skill. His fix is an explicit hierarchy-decomposition scaffold (generated as linked docs) that the agent walks to propose radical changes per component, plus plugging in specialized models (multimodal for image QC, high-reasoning for critique) as skills inside the loop.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before the optimization loop, prompt the agent to decompose the problem/codebase into a linked hierarchy of component docs (data, architecture, loss, metrics, scripts), then require it to propose improvements per component instead of hill-climbing the whole repo.

takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also review this of course um this plan uh with a with a adversarially and um or collaboratively with another agent or another model

takeaways.technique: Per-subtask model specialization inside the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Route each loop sub-step to the model best suited: multimodal model for image/visual QC, high test-time-compute reasoning model for hypothesis generation and critique, rather than one model for everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can kind of call in another model that has a better multimodal capability uh to review the image

takeaways.technique: Oracle-style packaged-context escalation for hard reviews
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a CLI that packages code plus data and sends it to a strong reasoning API to close the loop on outcomes and critique whether the implementation was effective.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Peter Spinberger's Oracle CLI which packages the code and package the data and send them to API

takeaways.technique: Explicit decomposition as a context-management primitive
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat decomposition into linked component docs as an explicit action so the agent reasons step-by-step through a small doc at a time instead of holding the whole codebase/objective in context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: decompose the problem into its subcomponents but it's an explicit act um um action

takeaways.technique: Qualitative/visual QC as an in-loop metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Where metrics are qualitative (image alignment, mask correctness), insert a model-based visual check as a loop metric so the agent can self-diagnose failures it otherwise couldn't see.
takeaways.evidence_quote: call in another model that has a better multimodal capability uh to review the image uh and what's the opinion about this image
